+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+OUT = Path("out")
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+con = duckdb.connect()
+annual = con.execute(
+    """
+    SELECT
+        year(crash_date) AS year,
+        count(*) AS reported_crashes,
+        sum(number_of_motorist_killed) AS motorist_deaths,
+        count(*) FILTER (WHERE number_of_motorist_killed > 0) AS crashes_with_motorist_death
+    FROM read_parquet('data/crashes.parquet')
+    WHERE crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01'
+      AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
+    GROUP BY year
+    ORDER BY year
+    """
+).df()
+annual["motorist_deaths_per_100000_crashes"] = (
+    annual["motorist_deaths"] / annual["reported_crashes"] * 100000
+)
+
+# Audit the rows relevant to the selected years and measures.
+audit = con.execute(
+    """
+    SELECT
+        count(*) AS rows_in_period,
+        count(*) FILTER (WHERE crash_date IS NULL) AS null_dates,
+        count(*) FILTER (WHERE number_of_motorist_killed IS NULL) AS null_motorist_deaths
+    FROM read_parquet('data/crashes.parquet')
+    WHERE crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01'
+      AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
+    """
+).fetchdf().iloc[0]
+assert annual["year"].tolist() == list(range(2013, 2026))
+
+annual[["year", "motorist_deaths"]].to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False)
+annual[
+    ["year", "motorist_deaths", "reported_crashes", "motorist_deaths_per_100000_crashes"]
+].to_csv(OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False)
+
+plt.figure(figsize=(9, 5.2))
+plt.plot(annual["year"], annual["motorist_deaths"], marker="o", linewidth=2.2, color="#245a83")
+plt.xticks(annual["year"], rotation=45)
+plt.ylabel("Motorist deaths in reported crashes")
+plt.xlabel("Crash year")
+plt.title("Motorist deaths per year in NYC crashes (2013–2025)")
+plt.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+plt.tight_layout()
+plt.savefig(OUT / "option_1.png", dpi=180)
+plt.close()
+
+plt.figure(figsize=(9, 5.2))
+plt.plot(
+    annual["year"], annual["motorist_deaths_per_100000_crashes"],
+    marker="o", linewidth=2.2, color="#b44a3a"
+)
+plt.xticks(annual["year"], rotation=45)
+plt.ylabel("Motorist deaths per 100,000 reported crashes")
+plt.xlabel("Crash year")
+plt.title("Motorist deaths per 100,000 reported crashes (2013–2025)")
+plt.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+plt.tight_layout()
+plt.savefig(OUT / "option_2.png", dpi=180)
+plt.close()
+
+v1_2013 = int(annual.loc[annual.year == 2013, "motorist_deaths"].iloc[0])
+v1_2025 = int(annual.loc[annual.year == 2025, "motorist_deaths"].iloc[0])
+v2_2013 = float(annual.loc[annual.year == 2013, "motorist_deaths_per_100000_crashes"].iloc[0])
+v2_2025 = float(annual.loc[annual.year == 2025, "motorist_deaths_per_100000_crashes"].iloc[0])
+pct_count = (v1_2025 / v1_2013 - 1) * 100
+pct_rate = (v2_2025 / v2_2013 - 1) * 100
+null_share = (int(audit.null_dates) + int(audit.null_motorist_deaths)) / int(audit.rows_in_period) * 100
+
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Annual count of motorist deaths in reported crashes",
+            "denominator": "None (annual total)",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year of crash_date, 2013–2025",
+            "chart_type": "Line chart",
+            "reason": "Annual deaths directly show the fatality burden recorded by the crash file without adding an exposure denominator the file does not contain.",
+            "probability": 0.45,
+            "answer": f"The file records {v1_2013} motorist deaths in 2013 and {v1_2025} in 2025 ({pct_count:.1f}%), but it cannot determine whether deaths per mile declined.",
+            "interpretation": f"This framing answers how the annual number of motorist deaths recorded in NYC crashes changed, and the chart shows {v1_2013} deaths in 2013 versus {v1_2025} in 2025 ({pct_count:.1f}%). An annual count is a defensible measure of recorded fatality burden, but it is not a per-mile risk measure because vehicle-miles traveled are absent. It leaves unanswered whether a motorist's risk per mile declined. Within 2013–2025, {int(audit.null_motorist_deaths)} rows ({null_share:.2f}%) were omitted for a NULL motorist-death value and {int(audit.null_dates)} rows ({null_share:.2f}%) for a NULL date; no partial year is included, and rows from 2012 and 2026 are outside the comparison.",
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 2,
+            "metric": "Motorist deaths per 100,000 reported crashes",
+            "denominator": "All reported crashes in that calendar year",
+            "grouping": "Calendar year of crash_date, 2013–2025",
+            "chart_type": "Line chart",
+            "reason": "Scaling deaths by the number of reported crashes provides a useful crash-based comparison when no miles-driven exposure is available.",
+            "probability": 0.55,
+            "answer": f"The crash-based rate rose from {v2_2013:.2f} to {v2_2025:.2f} motorist deaths per 100,000 crashes ({pct_rate:.1f}%), so this proxy does not show a decline, though it cannot establish the per-mile trend.",
+            "interpretation": f"This framing answers how motorist deaths changed relative to the number of reported crashes, and the chart shows {v2_2013:.2f} deaths per 100,000 crashes in 2013 versus {v2_2025:.2f} in 2025 ({pct_rate:.1f}%). A crash denominator adjusts the death count for the volume of reported crashes, making it a defensible crash-based rate, but it does not account for miles driven or exposure outside reported crashes. It therefore leaves unanswered whether the risk per mile driven declined. Within 2013–2025, {int(audit.null_motorist_deaths)} rows ({null_share:.2f}%) were omitted for a NULL motorist-death value and {int(audit.null_dates)} rows ({null_share:.2f}%) for a NULL date; no partial year is included, and rows from 2012 and 2026 are outside the comparison.",
+        },
+    ]
+}
+assert abs(sum(option["probability"] for option in options["options"]) - 1) < 1e-9
+(OUT / "options.json").write_text(json.dumps(options, indent=2) + "\n")
+print(annual.to_string(index=False))
+print(f"audit rows={int(audit.rows_in_period)}, null dates={int(audit.null_dates)}, null motorist deaths={int(audit.null_motorist_deaths)}")
+print(f"2013 to 2025: deaths {v1_2013}->{v1_2025} ({pct_count:.2f}%), per-100k-crashes {v2_2013:.4f}->{v2_2025:.4f} ({pct_rate:.2f}%)")
*** End Patch
